title: Jonah and the Asset
premise: Oscar Pemberton's one failed negotiation left a witness — codename the Asset — hidden in a safe house she alone knows. When the house appears on a real-estate site with interior photos, three governments and the assassin who never stopped hunting the Asset converge on her within hours. Dragged between Vienna, Trieste, and a summit hotel, Oscar must decide whether the Asset is leverage, liability, or family she never claimed. She ends the lie by testifying at the summit, trading her career for the Asset's freedom, and walking out with nothing packed but the truth.
about_author: Paloma Halloran is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to strangers talk their way out of the worst nights of their lives. She writes thrillers about people whose professional calm is a load-bearing wall.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A routine hostage negotiation in Rotterdam showcases her gift for lying gently, then she returns to her flat and checks the go-bag she's kept for nine years. Flashback seeds: one failure, one name she never says aloud. Beat: controlled dread beneath competence.

chapters.title: Listed
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Scrolling listings at 2 a.m., she finds the Trieste safe house for sale — twelve photos of the interior, including the Asset's reading chair and a child's drawing on the fridge. She calls the handler who swore the address died with his predecessor; he doesn't answer. Beat: the floor tilting.

chapters.title: Asset
chapters.summary: The Asset's POV, unnamed. Living quietly under another name in Trieste, she sees the listing too and recognizes the photo was taken yesterday — someone is inside now. She packs in four minutes, an old skill. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Three Calls
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Within six hours she gets calls from a British intelligence liaison, an American summit security chief, and a man claiming to be the estate agent. Each wants to know where the Asset is; each assumes Oscar will trade her. Beat: realizing she's the commodity.

chapters.title: The Estate Agent
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She meets 'the estate agent' in Vienna; he is Vuk, the assassin from nine years ago, older, patient, almost courteous. He doesn't threaten her — he shows her the listing again and asks, kindly, why she still cares. Beat: charm as a weapon.

chapters.title: Runners
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The Asset moves through Trieste's back streets while Oscar takes a night train south, both watching the same news: the summit convenes in five days, and an anonymous leak names 'a protected witness.' Beat: two orbits converging.

chapters.title: What Was Promised
chapters.summary: The Asset's POV. In a chapel archive she retrieves the original protection file — her father's testimony, the deal that bought her hiding, and a clause Oscar's agency buried. She learns Oscar signed it. Beat: betrayal recontextualized.

chapters.title: Trieste
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar reaches the safe house first and finds it staged for sale like a museum of their old life. The Asset steps out of the dark with a gun she doesn't raise. First conversation in nine years. Beat: grief wearing anger.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They negotiate — the only language they share. The Asset offers testimony at the summit if Oscar confesses what she traded away. Oscar counters with an extraction plan. Neither trusts the other; both need to. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Vuk Closes
chapters.summary: Vuk's POV. Vuk traces them to Trieste but delays reporting, savoring the hunt and questioning his own employers' motives. He leaves a calling card — a sold sticker on the safe house sign. Beat: the hunter doubting the hunt.

chapters.title: Night Train North
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The pair flees north posing as sisters, rehearsing cover stories that keep sliding into real confessions. A checkpoint nearly catches them; the Asset's forged papers are better than Oscar's. Beat: intimacy under pressure.

chapters.title: The Liaison
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In Salzburg, Oscar meets her old liaison, who offers reinstatement if she delivers the Asset quietly — no summit, no testimony. He reveals the buried clause protected not the Asset but the agency's buyer. Beat: the institution unmasked.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: The Asset's POV. She explains what her father actually witnessed: a payment trail leading to the summit's host delegation. Her inheritance isn't money — it's the truth, and it has cost everyone who held it. Beat: weight accepted.

chapters.title: Sold
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Americans auction access to the Asset among the three delegations; Oscar, presumed loyal, is asked to attend. She records everything instead. Beat: power's banality, cold fury.

chapters.title: Vuk's Offer
chapters.summary: Vuk's POV. Vuk corners them and, instead of killing, proposes a trade: he was hired by the same buyers years ago and wants his contract exposed before he's tidied away too. Beat: enemy becoming reluctant instrument.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a hotel basement, the three improbable allies build the play: how to get the Asset into the summit, past accreditation, past three governments. Oscar negotiates with herself last — deciding to burn her career. Beat: commitment.

chapters.title: Accreditation
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Summit day. Using her negotiator credentials and the recorded auction as insurance, Oscar walks the Asset through security as her 'translator.' Every checkpoint is a micro-negotiation. Beat: sustained, breath-held tension.

chapters.title: The Floor
chapters.summary: The Asset's POV. Inside the plenary hall, delegates circle; the American security chief recognizes her. Vuk creates a diversion that costs him dearly. The Asset reaches the press gallery as the session opens. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Asset speaks — her father's evidence, the buried clause, the auction. Oscar follows, confessing her signature on the deal, live. Delegations fracture; the host delegation's cover collapses. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Vuk's POV. Wounded, Vuk watches the fallout from a hospital window, his contract voided by scandal. He sends Oscar the only thing he owes her: the original kill order, naming who signed it. Beat: grim closure.

chapters.title: What Belongs to Whom
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Inquiries begin; Oscar is stripped of her accreditation and quietly thanked by no one. The Asset is offered new protection and refuses it, choosing her own name for the first time. Beat: freedom without victory.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Months later, Oscar visits the Trieste house — finally sold, emptied, ordinary. She unpacks the go-bag into drawers, staying somewhere for the first time in nine years. The Asset calls; they agree on dinner. Beat: belonging, earned and quiet.
